cards.text: Paul has been locked up in Caesarea for two years, and now there's a new governor: Porcius Festus, who took over from Felix (Acts 24:27). Just three days after Festus arrives in the province, he goes up from Caesarea to Jerusalem. THREE DAYS in and he's already on the road, friend, when three days into a new job I'm still asking where they keep the cookie sheets.

cards.question: Festus has just arrived in Jerusalem. Who presents a case against Paul to him there?

answers.text: The chief priests and Jewish leaders

cards.text: They urge Festus to grant them a concession against Paul by summoning him to Jerusalem. Sounds like a simple favor, but friend, it is NOT a simple favor.

cards.question: Why do the leaders want Festus to summon Paul from Caesarea to Jerusalem?

answers.text: To ambush and kill him on the way
To have him speak at the temple
To let the high priest question him

cards.question: The leaders ask Festus to bring Paul to Jerusalem. Festus agrees to do it.

cards.text: Festus tells them Paul is being held in Caesarea and he's going there soon himself, so some of their leaders can come down with him and accuse Paul there. Somebody's got to go tell the ambush crew the plans changed.
Festus spends no more than eight or ten days with them in Jerusalem. Then he heads back down to Caesarea.

cards.question: Festus is back in Caesarea. The next day, he sits on the judgment seat and orders that ___ be brought in.

cards.text: Paul is brought in, and the Jews who came down from Jerusalem stand all around him, bringing many serious charges. Friend, if that many people circled me and pointed, I'd confess to eating cookies I never even touched.

cards.question: The accusers from Jerusalem are able to prove the serious charges they bring against Paul.
Surrounded by his accusers, Paul makes his defense. What does Paul tell Festus?

answers.text: He broke a minor temple rule

cards.text: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, asks Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me on these charges?” Jerusalem. Friend, you and I both heard about that ambush, and I'm sitting here going, NO, NO, NO.

cards.question: Festus asks Paul to go up to Jerusalem for trial. Where does Paul say he ought to be tried?

answers.text: Before the judgment seat of Caesar
Before the high priest in Jerusalem

cards.question: Paul tells Festus he has done nothing wrong to the Jews, and Festus himself ___ it.

cards.text: Then Paul says if he's guilty of anything worthy of death, he doesn't refuse to die, but if there's no truth to the accusations, no one has the right to hand him over to them. Friend, I can't even own up to burning one batch without blaming the oven, and this man is putting his LIFE on the table.

cards.question: Paul says no one has the right to hand him over to his accusers. What does Paul do next?

answers.text: He asks for Lysias the commander

cards.question: Festus confers with his council, then turns down Paul's appeal to Caesar.

cards.text: Festus tells Paul, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!” Keep your apron on, friend, because Paul's road isn't done yet, and neither are we.

findings.problem: The setup line "Sounds like a simple favor, but friend, it is NOT a simple favor" tells the baker the request is sinister just before card 4 asks why the leaders want Paul summoned. That rules out the two harmless wrong answers, "To have him speak at the temple" and "To let the high priest question him," and leaves only the ambush.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the Festus quote, the fragment "Jerusalem." and the joke sentence. Non-opening story cards are limited to two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 12 ends with Papa Dorin shouting "NO, NO, NO" at the idea of Jerusalem, right before card 13 asks where Paul says he ought to be tried. Both wrong answers are Jerusalem options, so the setup rules them out and the right answer is the only non-Jerusalem choice.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers are "in Jerusalem" and differ only slightly from each other. The right answer is the one option that is not like the others, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out.

findings.problem: The question itself says Paul insists no one can hand him over to his accusers. That rules out the wrong answer "He calls on the Sanhedrin," because the Sanhedrin is his accusers' own council. Only two real options are left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Paul's defense in Acts 25:8 names three things he has not offended against: the law of the Jews, the temple and Caesar. No card mentions them, so the baker misses what the defense actually claims, including the mention of Caesar that leads to the appeal in v. 11.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
